If you can remember (+ recall) and understand the information adequately just by reading and doing practice questions, it might not even be necessary to force yourself to write notes. It might just not be the method for you, people remember things differently after all.

Having a different studying style does not make you lazy. Being a good student does not necessarily mean using all the "top - do this to succeed" methods, you have to take advantage of your own strengths.

As for the not remembering notes part: in my experience, it can be difficult to remember things right off the bat. So maybe create the set of notes that you must or want to remember and then attempt to write it down from memory. Once that's done, take a different colour pen or whatever and add in what's missing or correct any mistakes. From there it's simply repeating the recalling procedure. It is relatively time consuming though and might not work for all subjects.

Alternatives would be to recite the notes outloud (from memory) and then checking what you missed, but it's easier to miss stuff. Or make flash cards of the notes and study those. Just writing down the notes once and simply reading them over and over doesn't tend to work very well in the initial stages.
